title: Key transit routes
steps: Izumo Airport (IZO) → Matsue — airport limousine bus, departs ≈10 min after each arriving flight's baggage claim opens; confirm you're on the Matsue-route bus, not the Izumo-route one. Buy your ticket at the counter or on board.

Getting around Matsue — the Matsue Lake Line loop bus runs ≈every 30 min (full loop ≈50 min), {{fact:matsue-lake-line-ride-250-yen}} per ride or {{fact:matsue-lake-line-day-pass-700-yen}} for an all-day pass, and covers the station, the castle, the Horikawa boat dock, Shiomi Nawate, and Matsue Shinjiko Onsen — avoids stringing long walks between stops for the 2 low-mobility travelers.

Matsue → Izumo Taisha — Ichibata Electric Railway, Matsue Shinjiko Onsen Station to Izumo Taisha-mae, with a same-platform transfer at Kawato Station. ≈{{fact:ichibata-matsue-izumo-900-yen}} one way. ⚠ Don't count on tapping through: Ichibata is a private line and publishes nothing about ICOCA/Suica acceptance anywhere in its own fare pages (its fare table is a PDF, last revised Mar 2025) — buy paper tickets for the eight of you, and allow a minute at the window.

Matsue → Odashi (the base transfer, with luggage) — JR San-in Main Line, ≈45–90 min depending on train (limited express vs. local), {{fact:jr-sanin-matsue-odashi-fare}}. IC cards stop working at Izumo-shi Station — the JR West ICOCA area ends there, so buy a paper ticket (or top up with cash at the gate) before boarding past Izumo-shi.

Odashi Station → Iwami Ginzan / Omori — Iwami Kotsu community bus toward the World Heritage Center, ≈30 min, {{fact:odashi-omori-bus-760-yen}} one way, roughly hourly (with a documented gap around the 10 o'clock hour — don't assume a bus is always 30 minutes away). Carry cash: this is past the ICOCA boundary and nothing on the operator's or the World Heritage Center's pages promises IC acceptance out here. The World Heritage Center is not the village — the site's own Q&A puts it about five minutes by road from the Omori townscape, with a further bus leg between them, so check where your service actually terminates before boarding.

Omori townscape → Ryugenji Mabu mine entrance — the Ginzan Cart (Green Slow Mobility), a 6-seat electric cart, {{fact:ginzan-cart-500-yen}} one way depending on where you board, no reservations, first-come first-served, 8:00–18:00. The operator publishes 12–14 runs a day and no interval, so budget up to an hour for the next cart rather than the half-hour a group of 8 would like it to be. Closed Wednesdays and can suspend on short notice in bad weather. If it's full or not running, the walk is ≈2.3 km / 45 min one way on an unpaved forest trail — plan real time for this, not a placeholder, if traveling with the two low-mobility members of the group. A rental e-bike ({{fact:iwami-ginzan-ebike-700-yen}} for 2hr) from Rentacycle Kawamura by the Daikansho-mae plaza is a confirmed third option, and the operator recommends the electric bikes over ordinary ones because the valley road climbs.

Last practical return out of the valley (Iwami Ginzan day) — the deadline is the last Iwami Kotsu bus from Omori / the World Heritage Center toward Ota-shi, not a train: the trip sleeps on this side that night. ⚠ The timetable is seasonal and isn't published on the World Heritage Center's site — confirm the day's last departure at its information desk on arrival. Fallback if you miss it: the centre's transport page lists Ota-shi taxi firms — Fuji Daiichi Kotsu 0854-82-0660, Nihon Kotsu Ota office 0854-82-0456 — and eight people is two or three cars.
Omori/Odashi → Izumo Airport (departure day) — reverse the JR leg to Izumo-shi, then the airport limousine bus or a taxi for the final stretch; there's no direct rail into the airport itself.
